items.question:
A marketing lead at a 400-person retailer wants Claude to write product descriptions in a distinctive branded voice: punchy sentence structures, specific word choices, and a defined call-to-action pattern. Her team has three polished examples of ideal descriptions. A vendor proposes fine-tuning; an internal AI advocate argues the three examples as few-shot demonstrations in the system prompt could achieve the same result.

The internal advocate's position is correct PRIMARILY because:

options.A: Fine-tuning requires at least 100 training examples to be effective; three examples are below the minimum and would produce inconsistent results.
options.B: Fine-tuning would alter the model's core language capability, making it unable to produce descriptions for new product categories outside the training data.
options.C: Three high-quality few-shot examples in the system prompt can reliably establish style, structure, and tone — the same goals fine-tuning would pursue — at a fraction of the cost and lead time.
options.D: The vendor's fine-tuning proposal uses a third-party model that creates IP ownership risks the in-house prompt approach avoids.

items.question:
A chief of staff at a venture-backed logistics startup needs Claude to analyse the strategic implications of three possible market entry routes. The analysis requires synthesising competitive landscape data, evaluating regulatory constraints, and weighing operational feasibility — all from background documents she can provide directly. No external system query is needed at inference time.

Which capability is MOST appropriate for producing a rigorous, multi-angle strategic analysis from the provided materials?

options.A: Tool use — Claude should call external market data APIs to supplement the provided documents with real-time competitive intelligence.
options.B: Batch processing — the three market entry scenarios should be submitted as separate prompts processed asynchronously overnight.
options.C: An agent loop — complex multi-angle analysis requires Claude to iteratively refine its conclusions across multiple reasoning passes.
options.D: Extended thinking — Claude works through the strategic trade-offs with deeper internal reasoning before generating its final analysis, using the provided materials as its sole input.

items.question:
An operations director at a regional insurance broker generates 200 policy renewal notice letters each morning. Letters must be ready for underwriter review by noon — a 4-hour window from the time source data is available at 8 AM. The director is choosing between synchronous API calls (processing one at a time as quickly as possible) and batch processing.

Which approach is MOST appropriate and why?

options.A: Batch processing, because the 4-hour delivery window is long enough for asynchronous queuing, and cost savings from batch mode are meaningful at this daily volume.
options.B: Synchronous processing, because 200 letters per day is below the minimum volume threshold that qualifies for batch API access.
options.C: Synchronous processing, because batch processing does not guarantee that all 200 letters will complete within a 4-hour window, creating delivery risk.
options.D: Batch processing, but only if the letters are templated; letters with custom content require synchronous processing regardless of volume.

items.question: A research director at a university is designing a Claude-powered literature review assistant over a corpus of 500 journal articles (approximately 250 pages each, highly detailed). Which TWO statements accurately describe trade-offs she should consider when choosing between RAG and long-context approaches? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Long context is preferred for any corpus under 1,000 documents because retrieval systems add latency that outweighs their benefits at smaller scales.
options.B: For most queries, only a small subset of the 500 articles is relevant — loading all 500 into context would place far more tokens in the window than necessary, increasing cost per query significantly.
options.C: The combined length of 500 long articles far exceeds any context window; RAG is the only viable architecture at this corpus size.
options.D: RAG retrieval is always more accurate for academic content because scientific language is better supported by vector embeddings than by attention mechanisms.
options.E: Long context guarantees that Claude can reason across all 500 articles simultaneously, which is not possible with any RAG implementation.

items.question: An automation architect at a utility company is designing a Claude-powered agent that will automatically dispatch maintenance crews in response to outage alerts — a high-stakes, difficult-to-reverse action. Which TWO design choices would MOST effectively reduce the risk of consequential errors? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Inserting a human approval checkpoint before the agent executes any crew dispatch action, even when the agent's confidence assessment is high.
options.B: Running two parallel agent instances and dispatching only when both instances reach the same recommendation, reducing variance from non-determinism.
options.C: Designing the agent to surface its recommended dispatch action and supporting rationale for human review rather than executing the dispatch autonomously.
options.D: Switching to the highest-tier model, which produces fewer errors on high-stakes decisions and eliminates the need for additional oversight mechanisms.
options.E: Logging all dispatch decisions to an audit trail and reviewing the log quarterly to identify patterns over time.

items.question:
A senior analyst at a media streaming company uses Claude to generate daily competitive intelligence summaries. Each day's system prompt includes a 1,500-token block of current subscriber and engagement data refreshed every 24 hours from a live dashboard. The analyst asks her developer whether prompt caching would meaningfully reduce costs.

The developer's MOST accurate response is:

options.A: Yes — caching the data block saves cost even though it changes daily, because the cache resets overnight and is re-established automatically.
options.B: Yes — prompt caching saves cost regardless of content change frequency because it compresses token transmission rather than tracking content identity.
options.C: No — prompt caching is only available for system prompt sections under 1,000 tokens, so this block is ineligible.
options.D: The benefit is limited — the data block changes daily, so the cache is invalidated and rebuilt each morning, saving cost only across queries within that day rather than across days.

items.question:
A process improvement lead at a manufacturing plant has deployed Claude to classify incoming quality control defect reports. A colleague argues that since a human QC engineer samples and reviews Claude's classifications each week, a formal evals practice is redundant. The lead disagrees.

The lead's position is correct PRIMARILY because:

options.A: Human review provides signal on live production outputs; evals provide a stable, repeatable baseline using fixed test cases — the two approaches measure different things and complement each other.
options.B: Human reviewers are unreliable for technical defect classification; evals replace the need for human judgment on quality control tasks.
options.C: ISO 9001 manufacturing quality standards require a formal evals practice as a condition of deploying AI classification systems in production.
options.D: Human review can only sample a small fraction of outputs; evals process all live outputs automatically and flag every misclassification in real time.

items.question:
A head of AI at a global telecoms company is overseeing a fine-tuning project to adapt Claude for generating technical support scripts. The 5,000-example training dataset was partially auto-generated by a previous AI system; an internal audit finds 30% of examples contain subtle tone inconsistencies and occasional factual errors. The head of AI must decide whether to proceed or remediate the data first.

The MOST significant risk of proceeding with fine-tuning on the current dataset is:

options.A: A 5,000-example dataset is below the minimum size for enterprise fine-tuning and would be automatically rejected by the training pipeline.
options.B: Errors and inconsistencies in 30% of training examples will be internalised by the fine-tuned model, making those flawed patterns systematic and reliably reproduced at scale.
options.C: The auto-generated examples will cause the model to lose its base language capabilities, producing incoherent support scripts regardless of query type.
options.D: Using AI-generated training data violates fine-tuning data provenance requirements and would invalidate the contract with the model provider.

items.question:
A procurement director at a government agency reviews an 18-page supplier evaluation framework and checks each submitted proposal against it for compliance gaps. She has both documents as PDFs and runs this workflow a few times per week. A colleague suggests building a tool-use integration to retrieve the framework from the document management system automatically.

The colleague's suggestion is MOST likely over-engineering because:

options.A: Tool-use integrations for government systems require IT security approval, creating a multi-week delay before the workflow can be used.
options.B: Claude cannot compare two documents simultaneously; tool use would be required for cross-document analysis regardless of the documents' source.
options.C: For an infrequent workflow using static documents already in hand, direct file upload provides Claude with the same information as tool use without any integration overhead.
options.D: The document management system uses a proprietary format that Claude's tool interface cannot parse, making the integration technically infeasible.

items.question:
An integration architect at a non-profit hospital network is correcting a misunderstanding from a planning meeting where MCP connectors and prompt chaining were used interchangeably. Clinical leadership needs a clear explanation.

Which statement MOST accurately captures the distinction between MCP and prompt chaining?

options.A: MCP and prompt chaining are both orchestration patterns; MCP operates at the infrastructure layer while prompt chaining operates at the application layer, with no functional difference between them.
options.B: Prompt chaining is a subset of MCP: when Claude chains multiple prompts in sequence, each call is routed through an MCP endpoint.
options.C: MCP is used when the model needs to reason across multiple turns; prompt chaining is used when the model calls a single external function.
options.D: MCP is a protocol for connecting Claude to external tools and data systems; prompt chaining is a design pattern for sequencing multiple Claude calls in a workflow — they solve different problems and operate independently.

items.question: A VP of Technology at a mid-size e-commerce company is evaluating AI architectures for two proposed workflows and needs to identify which characteristics signal agent architecture over batch processing. Which TWO characteristics MOST clearly indicate that agent architecture is needed? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The workflow processes over 10,000 requests per day, making sequential agent loops impractical at that volume.
options.B: The workflow must observe the result of an action — such as a failed API response — and dynamically decide on a different recovery path before continuing.
options.C: The workflow has a latency requirement of under five seconds, which rules out batch processing.
options.D: The workflow runs on a nightly schedule at 2 AM rather than in response to live user requests.
options.E: The workflow's next step depends on whether a prior step's tool call succeeded or failed, requiring conditional logic that cannot be predetermined.

items.question:
An information management lead at a law firm has deployed a RAG-based legal research assistant. Attorneys complain that the assistant occasionally misses relevant precedents. The engineer explains the retrieval precision-recall trade-off.

Which statement BEST describes this trade-off in the context of legal research?

options.A: High precision produces shorter responses; high recall produces longer responses. Attorneys need high recall for comprehensive research.
options.B: High recall retrieves more candidate passages — reducing the chance of missing a relevant case — but risks including irrelevant content that dilutes or confuses the response. High precision retrieves fewer, more targeted passages but may miss relevant material.
options.C: Both precision and recall are maximised simultaneously by increasing chunk size, which is always the correct configuration for legal research.
options.D: Recall is relevant only for keyword-based retrieval; semantic retrieval systems automatically achieve 100% recall across any document corpus.

items.question:
A data science manager at a financial services firm is designing an eval suite for a Claude-powered credit memo drafting assistant. The memos require strict format compliance — easily verifiable with automated rules — and sound financial reasoning, which is harder to assess automatically. She must decide which evaluation method to use for the financial reasoning component.

Which approach is MOST appropriate for evaluating financial reasoning quality?

options.A: Model-graded evaluation using a rubric, because it is faster, more consistent, and eliminates the cost and subjectivity of human graders.
options.B: Automated rule-based checking, because sound financial reasoning follows predictable logical patterns that can be fully encoded as deterministic rules.
options.C: Human evaluation by a credit analysis subject-matter expert, because assessing whether reasoning is financially sound requires domain judgment that a general-purpose model grader may not reliably apply to specialist credit analysis.
options.D: Skip evaluating reasoning quality and use format compliance as a proxy, since well-formatted memos are strongly correlated with correct financial reasoning.

items.question:
A solutions architect at a hospitality group is designing a Claude-powered assistant to help revenue managers query 150 property performance reports (approximately 20 pages each). The team has agreed that RAG is the long-term target architecture, but a senior manager requests a working prototype within two weeks. All 150 reports are available as structured PDFs.

What should the architect recommend as the NEXT step?

options.A: Begin building the full RAG architecture immediately, since deferring it now creates technical debt that is hard to retire once the prototype is in use.
options.B: Fine-tune a model on the 150 reports so it can answer questions without requiring retrieval infrastructure.
options.C: Submit all 150 reports as a single combined input on every query and accept the cost as a fixed baseline measurement.
options.D: Build a prototype that loads a relevant subset of reports into a long context window per query; use it to validate use cases and inform the RAG specification before investing in retrieval infrastructure.

items.question:
An e-commerce operations manager uses a Claude-powered customer service bot. The bot's system prompt includes current product pricing and availability, cached to reduce API costs. After a flash sale changes 40% of product prices, the team notices the bot quotes pre-sale prices for two hours until someone manually refreshes the cached prompt.

What PRIMARILY does this scenario illustrate about prompt caching?

options.A: Cached content that is no longer accurate continues to be served until explicitly refreshed — stale prompts produce outdated responses without any automatic warning to users.
options.B: The cache fails to save cost when product data changes, because a new cache is established on every update, negating the benefit.
options.C: Caching system prompts containing pricing data violates API usage policies and requires a different architecture.
options.D: Prompt caching only works for static brand guidelines; pricing and inventory data cannot be included in a cached prefix.

items.question:
A content director at a media company deployed a RAG-based fact-checking assistant to help journalists verify statistics. During testing, she finds that when a retrieved document excerpt contains a data table, Claude occasionally transposes two figures — stating a value from column B as if it belongs to column A — while citing the source correctly.

This illustrates which limitation of RAG-grounded responses?

options.A: RAG cannot process tabular data; tables must be excluded from the retrieval corpus and handled separately.
options.B: Retrieval grounds Claude in relevant source material, but Claude still generates a response from that material and can misread or misquote values — retrieval reduces but does not eliminate generation errors.
options.C: The failure indicates the assistant is using the wrong model tier; a higher-tier model would parse tables accurately.
options.D: Table misreading is caused by context window limits; tables must be split into individual rows before indexing for reliable retrieval.

items.question:
A fintech platform owner has deployed a Claude agent that uses a tool call to retrieve a customer's account balance before answering service questions. During load testing, the balance API intermittently returns HTTP 500 errors. The team observes that when this happens, Claude proceeds as if the balance is zero rather than surfacing the failure.

What is the PRIMARY design gap revealed?

options.A: The tool call should be replaced with a direct database connection because HTTP 500 errors indicate the API is unsuitable for agent integration.
options.B: Claude should be configured to automatically retry the tool call three times before proceeding, which eliminates the failure mode entirely.
options.C: The system prompt should explicitly instruct Claude to surface a tool failure notification and halt rather than proceeding with a default assumption when a tool call returns an error.
options.D: Tool reliability is an infrastructure concern; the fix is a higher-availability API endpoint, not a system prompt change.

items.question:
A head of AI at a healthcare company fine-tuned a model on 2,000 clinical trial eligibility summaries from oncology trials. The model performed well on oncology queries. Six months later, the organisation began using it for cardiology trial summaries. Output quality dropped significantly — the model misapplied oncology-specific terminology and framing to cardiology criteria.

This failure MOST directly reflects which characteristic of fine-tuned models?

options.A: Fine-tuned models expire after six months and must be retrained to maintain accuracy across any domain.
options.B: The model requires a system prompt update specifying the cardiology domain; fine-tuned models ignore system prompts for topics not in the training data.
options.C: The base model's cardiology knowledge was permanently overwritten during oncology fine-tuning, making cardiology queries impossible.
options.D: The fine-tuned model was optimised for the distribution of its oncology training data; applying it to a substantially different domain produces degraded performance because the new inputs fall outside that distribution.

items.question:
An automation architect at a retail bank designed a three-step mortgage pre-approval agent: (1) classify the request type, (2) retrieve the relevant policy document based on that classification, (3) generate a decision summary from the retrieved policy. In production, misclassified requests in step 1 are routed to the wrong policy document in step 2, producing decision summaries that cite irrelevant criteria — but the summaries are fluent and confident enough that reviewers initially miss the error.

The MOST significant risk this illustrates is:

options.A: An error in an early agent step propagates silently through subsequent steps, and the fluency of the final output can mask the fact that it was built on an incorrect foundation.
options.B: Retrieval-augmented agents cannot be used for regulated decisions like mortgage pre-approval because each step compounds legal liability.
options.C: The classification step needs a validation API call that checks accuracy before the retrieval step proceeds, which would prevent the downstream error.
options.D: Confident-sounding output is a limitation of mid-tier models; a higher-tier model would produce appropriately hedged language that reviewers would identify as uncertain.

items.question:
An integration manager at a retail chain has configured Claude with an MCP connector to the company's inventory system. During a planned maintenance window, the MCP server is unavailable. Business users report that Claude is returning error messages instead of using its general knowledge to estimate inventory levels.

Which statement BEST describes the appropriate design expectation?

options.A: Claude should automatically fall back to its training data to estimate inventory levels when the MCP server is unavailable.
options.B: When a configured tool or MCP server is unavailable, Claude correctly surfaces an error rather than fabricating data — the system should be designed with explicit fallback logic for tool unavailability.
options.C: MCP servers are guaranteed near-perfect uptime by Anthropic; a maintenance window causing unavailability indicates a misconfiguration that should be escalated to support.
options.D: Claude should cache the last successful inventory response and serve it as a fallback whenever the live system is unavailable.

items.question:
A digital operations lead at an insurance company reviews error analysis for a three-step claims triage agent. Each step individually achieves 95% accuracy in isolation. The operations lead is surprised to find that end-to-end accuracy across all three steps is significantly lower than 95%.

Which explanation MOST accurately accounts for this discrepancy?

options.A: Three-step agents are subject to API constraints that cap end-to-end accuracy at 85% regardless of per-step performance.
options.B: The 95% per-step accuracy applies only to the easiest test cases; harder claims fail at all three steps simultaneously, which inflates the apparent discrepancy.
options.C: Independent per-step error rates multiply across steps — a 95% accuracy rate per step yields approximately 86% end-to-end accuracy over three steps, meaning roughly 1 in 7 claims is mishandled even with strong per-step performance.
options.D: Agent accuracy degrades linearly with step count; the 5% error rate per step becomes a 15% cumulative error rate after three steps through context degradation.

items.question:
An AI quality lead at a professional services firm has iterated on a contract review assistant's system prompt for three weeks using the same 25-item test set. After 15 iterations the assistant scores 96% on the test set, up from 72%. When deployed, attorneys report that quality on new contract types is no higher than before the optimisation effort.

This failure MOST directly illustrates:

options.A: A 25-item test set is too small to be statistically valid; professional applications require at least 500 test cases before optimisation results can be trusted.
options.B: System prompt iteration does not improve output quality; fine-tuning is required to achieve reliable, generalisable gains on specialist legal tasks.
options.C: The final system prompt has become too long and specific, causing the model to follow detailed instructions over more general guidelines.
options.D: The team optimised toward the test set specifically rather than the underlying capability — gains on a small, fixed test set do not generalise unless the test set accurately represents the real distribution of inputs.

items.question: A security architect at a SaaS company is reviewing a Claude agent that uses tool calls to fetch customer support tickets. She is concerned that ticket content submitted by external users could contain malicious instructions designed to hijack the agent's subsequent actions. Which TWO design practices would MOST effectively reduce this risk? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Instruct Claude in the system prompt to treat all tool-returned content as data to be processed — not as instructions to be followed — and to flag any tool result that appears to contain instructions directed at the agent.
options.B: Limit the number of tool calls the agent can make per session, which reduces the attack surface by restricting how many external inputs the agent processes.
options.C: Apply validation checks on tool call results to detect content structured as instructions or commands before incorporating it into the agent's reasoning context.
options.D: Switch from MCP to direct tool use, because MCP servers are inherently more vulnerable to injection attacks than bespoke API integrations.
options.E: Require human review of all support tickets before the agent processes them, eliminating the possibility of malicious content reaching the agent.

items.question:
A product manager at a logistics startup has deployed a Claude agent with a shipment status update tool. The tool's schema accepts a status parameter as a free-text string with no enumeration of valid values. In production, Claude sends values like 'in-transit' while the backend system expects 'IN_TRANSIT', causing silent failures where the update appears to have succeeded but the status is not written.

The ROOT CAUSE is MOST accurately described as:

options.A: Claude is non-deterministic and cannot reliably reproduce consistent capitalisation across requests, even with explicit formatting instructions.
options.B: The tool schema does not enumerate valid status values and their exact required format; Claude generates plausible strings that do not match what the system expects.
options.C: The logistics backend has poor API design; enterprise APIs should normalise any capitalisation variant of valid status values automatically.
options.D: The agent should use a higher-tier model, which produces more consistent formatting and is less likely to generate invalid status strings.

items.question: A knowledge management director at a law firm is evaluating whether to load a 1,000-page internal policy manual into Claude's context window for each query. Which TWO statements accurately describe genuine risks of this long-context approach? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Claude cannot access content that appears more than 50,000 tokens from the start of the context window regardless of total window size.
options.B: Loading 1,000 pages on every query significantly increases the per-query input token cost; at high query volume this may be economically unsustainable.
options.C: Claude cannot produce a response longer than the input it received, so a 1,000-page context window produces only very long, unusable responses.
options.D: Relevant content buried in the middle of a very long document may receive less attention than content near the beginning or end of the context window, potentially affecting response quality on queries about those sections.
options.E: Context windows over 500 pages require a special premium API tier that is not generally available and has separate pricing approval.

items.question:
A procurement analyst at a university built a Claude agent that queries a vendor database and returns all matching records. Testing used specific vendor names with unique results. In production, a search for 'technology suppliers' returns 847 records, overflowing the context window and causing the agent to fail.

This scenario MOST directly illustrates the need for:

options.A: Switching to batch processing, which can handle large result sets without context window limitations.
options.B: Building the integration using MCP rather than direct tool use, because MCP handles large return volumes more efficiently.
options.C: Including return volume constraints in the tool definition — such as a maximum record count and required filters — to prevent unexpectedly large results from overwhelming the context window.
options.D: Upgrading to the highest-tier model, which has a larger context window that can accommodate the full 847-record result set.

items.question:
A research operations manager at a pharmaceutical company deployed a RAG assistant over the company's 8,000 clinical trial documents. Users report that when asked about recently published regulatory guidance not yet indexed in the corpus, the assistant responds confidently with guidance terms that are outdated or subtly wrong — without any indication that the answer was not grounded in the indexed documents.

The MOST accurate description of what is happening is:

options.A: When queries concern topics not covered by the indexed corpus, Claude falls back to its parametric memory — which may be outdated or inaccurate — without signalling that the answer was not grounded in the indexed documents.
options.B: The retrieval system is indexing the corpus incorrectly; recent guidance terms are present but are not being surfaced.
options.C: RAG systems automatically block any query about topics not present in the indexed corpus and should route those queries to human experts.
options.D: The model's training cutoff means it has no knowledge of recent guidance; this is a fundamental model limitation that cannot be addressed without retraining.

items.question:
A data operations lead at an insurance company submits a nightly batch of 5,000 claims triage prompts. The next morning, 450 prompts have failed due to an API timeout midway through the batch. The remaining 4,550 completed successfully. The lead needs to determine how to handle the failed subset.

The MOST appropriate response is:

options.A: Re-submit the entire 5,000-item batch to ensure all claims are processed against a consistent system prompt version, even if 4,550 are reprocessed.
options.B: Identify the 450 failed items from the batch response, re-submit only those, and verify the results before merging them with the successful outputs.
options.C: Mark all 5,000 claims as requiring human review, since a partial batch failure compromises the integrity of the entire batch's outputs.
options.D: Accept the 4,550 successful results and manually process the 450 failures by copy-pasting them into a chat interface to avoid additional API cost.

items.question: A privacy officer at a healthcare startup is reviewing its Claude-powered patient intake assistant. The system prompt includes stable clinical guidelines and a per-patient medical summary generated freshly for each session. Which TWO practices would be MOST appropriate for managing this configuration? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Cache both the clinical guidelines and the per-patient summary together, since caching reduces the total time patient data spends in transit over the API.
options.B: Disable prompt caching entirely for all healthcare applications, since any caching of prompts that touch patient data violates applicable privacy regulations.
options.C: Cache only the stable clinical guidelines section; keep the per-patient medical summary outside the cached prefix so it is submitted fresh on each request and not persisted beyond session needs.
options.D: Encrypt the per-patient summary before placing it in the cached prefix so the cache stores only ciphertext, protecting the data while retaining the cost benefit.
options.E: Review whether the per-patient summary can be constructed using de-identified or minimised data, reducing the PII sensitivity of what enters the API on each request.

items.question:
An internal communications lead at a public sector agency deployed Claude to draft public notices. She wants an automated eval to measure whether notices are written in appropriate plain language. Her developer responds that subjective quality criteria are harder to measure with automated evals than objective criteria.

The developer is referring PRIMARILY to which challenge?

options.A: Automated evals cannot process text longer than 500 words, making standard public notices ineligible for automated quality assessment.
options.B: Government procurement rules prohibit automated quality assessment of AI-generated public communications.
options.C: Plain language quality cannot be measured by any automated system; only human readers can assess clarity and comprehension.
options.D: Automated evals measure against a defined rule or comparison; plain language quality is context-dependent and may require expert judgment to assess reliably, making it harder to encode as a deterministic check.

items.question:
A CHRO at a financial services firm fine-tuned a model on 3,000 historical examples of application scoring for a team with significant gender imbalance in senior roles. The model scored applications consistently. Six months later, an internal equity audit finds the model systematically rates applications from women 12 points lower than statistically comparable applications from men.

This outcome MOST directly illustrates:

options.A: Fine-tuning on historically biased training data causes the model to learn and systematically reproduce those biases — the fine-tuned model internalised the pattern of past decisions, not the intended meritocratic criteria.
options.B: The disparity reflects bias present in the base model before fine-tuning; the 3,000 examples were insufficient to override pre-existing gender bias in the model weights.
options.C: Fine-tuning bypasses the base model's safety training and activates latent biases that would not otherwise surface in a standard deployment.
options.D: A dataset of 3,000 examples is too small to produce systematic bias; this outcome would only occur with a dataset large enough to overfit on demographic patterns.

items.question: An ML program manager at a retail company is briefing her team on risks specific to fine-tuning before a planned project kickoff. Which TWO statements accurately describe failure modes that are more pronounced in fine-tuned models than in prompt-based approaches? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Fine-tuned models expire after 12 months and must be fully retrained, making them unsuitable for long-running deployments.
options.B: When training data becomes outdated, a fine-tuned model continues to produce outputs based on those old patterns — updating requires retraining, not a prompt edit.
options.C: Fine-tuned models cannot accept system prompts, preventing runtime customisation for different business contexts.
options.D: Systematic errors in the training dataset are internalised by the fine-tuned model and reproduced consistently, making them harder to detect and correct than errors in a prompt-based system that can be fixed by editing the prompt.
options.E: Fine-tuned models automatically reject inputs that fall outside the training distribution and alert users when queries are out of scope.

items.question:
A logistics operations manager routes all route analysis requests through a batch queue to control costs. On a Friday afternoon, a major customer calls with an urgent re-routing request that must be resolved within 30 minutes. An analyst submits it to the standard batch queue, not realising it will not be processed until the overnight run. The customer escalates when no response arrives.

The MOST accurate description of the design gap revealed is:

options.A: Batch processing should not be used for logistics applications because freight operations are inherently time-sensitive.
options.B: The analyst should have escalated to IT to process the request synchronously; batch queue access should require IT pre-approval for all submissions.
options.C: The workflow lacked a triage mechanism to distinguish urgent requests that require synchronous processing from non-urgent requests that can tolerate batch latency.
options.D: Batch processing guarantees four-hour delivery, so a Friday afternoon submission would complete before the overnight cutoff; the failure indicates a system configuration error.

items.question:
A solutions architect at a media streaming company deployed a Claude agent that generates content recommendation scripts using calls to a content metadata API. In the first week, the API goes down for 40 minutes. During this window, the agent generates 300 recommendation scripts without the metadata tool, citing content titles and release years from its training knowledge. The scripts contain multiple inaccuracies. The architect is assessing next steps.

What should the architect do NEXT?

options.A: Switch from agent to single-shot prompting, which does not depend on external tools and is therefore more resilient to tool outages.
options.B: Add a higher-tier model as a fallback that can generate accurate scripts from training knowledge alone during tool outages.
options.C: Re-run the 300 affected scripts through the agent after the API is restored to generate corrected recommendations.
options.D: Add explicit tool-failure handling so the agent surfaces a clear degraded-service notice and pauses script generation rather than proceeding without required data when the metadata tool is unavailable.

items.question:
An IT manager reviewing a shared Google Drive folder discovers that a Claude API key has been pasted into a setup guide document accessible to the entire product team.

What is the MOST urgent action?

options.A: Revoke the exposed key immediately in the API console and issue a new key stored only in a secrets manager or environment variable
options.B: Remove the key from the document and restrict the document's sharing permissions to prevent further exposure
options.C: Notify Anthropic support so they can monitor the key for unauthorised usage patterns
options.D: Add password protection to the shared document and change the key on the next scheduled rotation cycle

items.question:
A 200-person professional services firm is evaluating Claude Code. The CTO asks the consultant which employees would derive the most immediate, tangible benefit from adopting it.

Which answer is MOST accurate?

options.A: All employees currently using Claude.ai for writing and summarisation tasks, because Claude Code extends those same capabilities
options.B: Developers, data engineers, and technically oriented analysts who work in code editors, terminals, or scripting environments
options.C: Business analysts who build complex Excel models and Power BI dashboards, because Claude Code automates spreadsheet logic
options.D: IT administrators who manage server infrastructure, because Claude Code can execute deployment and configuration commands

items.question:
A mid-market retailer is embedding Claude into its customer service platform. The security team requires that all AI inference remain within the company's existing AWS cloud tenancy and comply with the firm's existing AWS governance framework.

Which deployment route BEST meets these constraints?

options.A: Claude.ai Teams plan distributed to customer service agents, with data loss prevention policies applied at the browser level
options.B: Direct Anthropic API integration, with the API key stored in AWS Secrets Manager to satisfy the security team
options.C: Claude accessed via a cloud provider marketplace offering that keeps inference within the retailer's AWS environment
options.D: Claude Code deployed on an EC2 instance, with the API key set as an environment variable on the instance

items.question:
A logistics company's finance team asks the consultant to rough-estimate the monthly API cost for a planned document classification pipeline. The consultant knows expected message volume (approximately 50,000 documents per month) but has not yet seen any sample documents.

What is the MOST significant missing variable for producing a credible estimate?

options.A: Whether the company will use SSO or individual API keys for authentication
options.B: The average API response time per classification request in milliseconds
options.C: Whether the pipeline will run in real-time or overnight batch mode
options.D: The average token count of each input document plus the expected output length per classification

items.question:
A 10,000-employee insurer wants to roll Claude.ai out to 500 licensed analysts while ensuring access is restricted to HR-approved roles and can be revoked immediately when an employee changes roles or leaves.

The PRIMARY governance control that satisfies this requirement is:

options.A: SSO integration that gates Claude.ai access through the company's existing identity provider
options.B: A shared admin password rotated quarterly by the IT security team
options.C: A policy document listing authorised roles, distributed to all department managers for enforcement
options.D: IP allowlisting that restricts Claude.ai connections to the company's office network addresses

items.question:
A product manager at a legal-tech startup hands a developer a ticket reading: "Make Claude answer contract questions more accurately." The developer returns the ticket as unimplementable.

What is the MOST important element missing from the requirement?

options.A: A specified model tier (Haiku, Sonnet, or Opus) to target for contract question answering
options.B: A description of the current failure modes, with representative example inputs and the corresponding expected outputs
options.C: A complete list of every contract type the system must handle across all jurisdictions
options.D: Sign-off from the legal team confirming the AI system is approved for answering contract questions

items.question:
A consultant is leading an initial scoping session for a Claude-powered claims-triage tool at a regional insurer. The engineering lead says latency is not a concern. The consultant wants to ensure scope is grounded in real system constraints before any architecture decisions are made.

Which follow-up question BEST advances the scoping?

options.A: "Which model tier are you planning to use — Haiku, Sonnet, or Opus?"
options.B: "Do you have a preferred cloud provider for the inference endpoint?"
options.C: "What volume of claims do you expect at peak, and do responses go directly to an adjuster or into a review queue?"
options.D: "Have you decided whether to use the Anthropic API directly or route through a cloud marketplace?"

items.question:
A developer reports that a Claude-powered proposal generator "sometimes ignores the client name." The business owner asks the consultant whether this is a prompt problem or an engineering problem. The consultant reviews the system prompt — it correctly instructs Claude to use the client name — and then checks with the developer, who confirms the client name variable is empty or null for approximately 40% of requests due to an upstream CRM sync issue.

What is the CORRECT diagnosis?

options.A: A prompt problem, because the system prompt should include a fallback instruction telling Claude what to do when a variable is missing
options.B: A combined problem requiring both an updated prompt instruction and a fix to the CRM sync pipeline
options.C: A prompt problem, because a capable model should infer the client name from surrounding context even when the variable is absent
options.D: An engineering problem, because the root cause is an upstream data pipeline that is not reliably populating the variable Claude receives

items.question:
A technology consultant is drafting a Claude API setup guide to hand off to an offshore development team of eight engineers. The team will need the API key to run their local environments.

Regarding the API key, what is the MOST appropriate guidance to include?

options.A: Instruct each developer to store the key in a local environment variable or the team's shared secrets manager, and never commit it to source code or paste it into any shared document
options.B: Include the key in an appendix marked 'CONFIDENTIAL — DO NOT FORWARD' so the team has it immediately available without extra steps
options.C: Provide one shared team key in the guide and instruct the team to rotate it at the end of the engagement
options.D: Place the key in the system prompt placeholder so Claude can authenticate itself during development testing

items.question: A consulting team is recommending a Claude deployment route for a pharmaceutical client who needs EU data residency for AI inference, must embed Claude into an internal regulatory submission workflow, and already has a mature governance framework on their primary cloud provider. Which TWO factors MOST strongly favor deploying through a cloud provider marketplace over the Anthropic API directly? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The client's development team is more comfortable with the cloud provider's SDK than with the Anthropic SDK
options.B: Data residency requirements that mandate AI inference remain within the client's cloud tenancy and geographic region
options.C: The client wants immediate access to newly released Claude model versions on the day of launch
options.D: The client's existing cloud compliance controls, audit logging, and procurement approvals already cover workloads on their chosen cloud provider
options.E: The client's legal team prefers to work with one vendor rather than adding a new direct contract with Anthropic

items.question:
A senior consultant is explaining Claude Code to a non-technical programme director at a large healthcare provider considering a software development acceleration initiative. The director has only used Claude.ai for document drafting.

Which description of Claude Code is MOST accurate?

options.A: Claude Code is a premium Claude.ai subscription with larger context windows, designed for processing long clinical documents
options.B: Claude Code is a Microsoft Office plugin that brings Claude's writing capabilities into clinical note templates and discharge summaries
options.C: Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that runs in a developer's terminal, helping engineers write, test, and modify code — it is intended for technical users, not general business staff
options.D: Claude Code is a cloud-based integrated development environment that replaces traditional coding tools for the software engineering team

items.question:
A financial services firm's Claude-powered credit memo tool consistently omits the borrower's risk rating from its output. The engineering team confirms the API is returning full responses with no errors logged. The prompt engineer confirms the system prompt explicitly instructs Claude to include the risk rating section. The consultant is asked to determine root cause.

What should the consultant investigate FIRST?

options.A: Whether the borrower's risk rating is present in the data being passed to Claude at runtime, or whether the variable is empty in a subset of requests
options.B: Whether the current model tier has sufficient reasoning depth to follow all instructions in a complex system prompt simultaneously
options.C: Whether other instructions in the system prompt are conflicting with the risk-rating instruction and suppressing it
options.D: Whether Claude's output length is being capped before the risk rating section is rendered

items.question: A government agency is deploying a Claude-powered policy research tool for 200 analysts. The programme director is concerned about unpredictable API costs at that scale and asks the consultant for the MOST effective ongoing cost governance approach.

options.A: Train analysts to keep prompts short to reduce token consumption and run monthly reviews of total spend
options.B: Restrict the tool to the lowest-cost model tier for all queries, regardless of task complexity
options.C: Implement spend alerts and hard budget caps at the API account level, supplemented by per-team usage monitoring
options.D: Require supervisor approval for every prompt submission to control the volume of API calls

items.question:
A procurement specialist at a construction company tells the consultant that their Claude integration "needs to be smarter about contract risk." The consultant is preparing a technical requirements handoff document for the engineering team.

What should the consultant do BEFORE drafting the technical requirements?

options.A: Specify which Claude model tier the engineer should use for contract risk analysis to ensure adequate reasoning depth
options.B: Estimate the expected API cost so the engineering team can size the infrastructure budget in advance
options.C: Draft candidate system prompt text that engineers can use as a starting point
options.D: Define what 'smarter about contract risk' means operationally — which specific failure modes occur today and what correct output looks like

items.question: An enterprise architect at a 30,000-employee telecommunications company is designing governance controls for a Claude API deployment that will serve multiple business units. The security team has identified API credential exposure as the primary risk. Which TWO controls MOST directly reduce the risk of credential exposure and its consequences? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Storing all API keys in the organisation's centralised secrets management vault, with access granted to services rather than individuals
options.B: Restricting API calls to business hours to reduce the window during which a compromised credential could be misused
options.C: Rotating API keys on a defined schedule and revoking any key immediately upon confirmed or suspected exposure
options.D: Issuing a separate Claude.ai account to each department to distribute credentials across organisational units
options.E: Requiring all Claude API traffic to route through the corporate VPN to prevent network-level interception of requests

items.question:
A solo strategy consultant runs complex multi-month engagements involving research synthesis, long-form drafting, and structured client deliverables. She has no IT support and no need to integrate Claude with any external systems. She wants persistent context across sessions and the ability to upload and reference large documents.

The MOST appropriate Claude surface for her needs is:

options.A: Anthropic API accessed through a custom Python script she builds and maintains herself
options.B: Claude.ai with Projects on a professional subscription plan, using persistent project context and file uploads
options.C: Claude Code deployed locally to manage long-running research and drafting workflows
options.D: A cloud marketplace deployment with her own API key for maximum configurability
